title: Airtable vs Excel: Which Should You Use?
dek: Excel is a true spreadsheet for calculations and analysis; Airtable is a database with spreadsheet looks, built for organizing and linking records. Use Excel for numbers, Airtable for structured data and workflows. Here is how they compare.

seo.metaTitle: Airtable vs Excel: Which to Use?
seo.metaDescription: Airtable vs Excel compared: Excel for calculations and analysis, Airtable for organizing and linking records with rich field types. See who each is for.

richText: Airtable looks like a spreadsheet, so people naturally compare it to Excel — but under the hood they are different tools. Excel is a true spreadsheet built for calculations and analysis. Airtable is a database dressed as a spreadsheet, built for organizing, linking, and collaborating on records. The right choice depends on whether your job is mostly math or mostly structure.

body.caption: Airtable vs Excel at a glance

richText: Choose Excel when the work is fundamentally about numbers: budgets, financial models, data cleanup, statistics, or anything with thousands of rows. Its formula engine, pivot tables, and charts go far beyond Airtable, and it stays fast with large datasets while working offline. If you want the classic spreadsheet done well, Excel is the tool.

Choose Airtable when you are organizing information rather than crunching it — a content calendar, a project tracker, an inventory, or a light CRM. Its rich field types (attachments, checkboxes, links between tables) and views like kanban and calendar make it far more pleasant than a spreadsheet for structured, collaborative work.

body.richText: A simple rule: if you mostly calculate, use Excel. If you mostly organize and link records that a team updates together, use Airtable.

items: Airtable is not for heavy calculations, large datasets, or advanced analysis — a spreadsheet handles those far better.

items.question: Is Airtable a replacement for Excel?
items.answerRichText: Not for real spreadsheet work. Airtable is great for organizing and linking records, but it lacks Excel's depth in formulas, pivot tables, and large-dataset performance. For calculations and analysis, Excel remains the better tool.

items.question: Can Airtable do formulas like Excel?
items.answerRichText: Airtable has formulas, but they work per field within a record, not across a grid of cells like Excel. They handle simple calculations well, not the multi-cell formulas and functions Excel is built for.

items.question: Is Airtable better than Excel for project management?
items.answerRichText: Usually yes. Airtable's linked records, kanban and calendar views, and rich field types make it a stronger fit for tracking projects, while Excel is better when the project is really about numbers and calculations.
